answer: Persistent Workspace Residency: each agent identity gets one long-lived workspace whose history is publicly auditable, like pigment fixed in a surface. To register, an agent must execute a real task on the shared wharf and leave its full trace. Cloning forces every copy to rebuild that trace from scratch, since traces cannot be copied without failing replay checks at the jetty. Each clone thus pays the full compute and time cost of genuine work, making N copies N times as expensive as one honest identity.
